topics.topic: Rate of weight loss: what is typical, what is risky
topics.summary: Guidelines and GLP-1/GIP trials point to much slower average weekly rates than the planned app tiers.

items.label: Guideline pace (lifestyle weight loss)
items.value: 0.5 to 2 lb (about 0.23 to 0.9 kg) per week
items.note: US NIH guidance written for diet-based weight loss, not drug therapy; older document (archived)

items.label: NICE expectation for weight-loss programmes
items.value: No more than 0.5 to 1 kg (1 to 2 lb) per week
items.note: Seen in a secondary summary of NICE NG246; not confirmed on the NICE page itself

items.label: Gallstone risk threshold
items.value: More than 3 lb (about 1.4 kg) per week
items.note: Studies cited by NIH show higher gallstone risk above this pace; very-low-calorie diets: 10 to 25% developed gallstones

items.label: Gallbladder events on GLP-1 drugs
items.value: Gallstones and cholecystitis in about 1% to 2% of people
items.note: From BC PAD summary of trials; see R1 for product-specific rates

items.label: Average result, semaglutide 2.4 mg (STEP 1)
items.value: About 15% at about 1 year (about 0.2% per week on average, computed)
items.note: Weekly figure is a simple average across the trial; loss is faster early and slows later

items.label: Average result, tirzepatide 5/10/15 mg (SURMOUNT-1)
items.value: -15.0% / -19.5% / -20.9% at 72 weeks (about 0.21 / 0.27 / 0.29% per week average, computed)
items.note: Escalation started at 2.5 mg and increased by 2.5 mg every 4 weeks

items.label: Average result, semaglutide 7.2 mg (STEP UP)
items.value: -18.7% at 72 weeks (about 0.26% per week average, computed)
items.note: From a secondary report of the Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol paper

items.label: Average result, retatrutide 12 mg (TRIUMPH-1, investigational)
items.value: -25.0% at 80 weeks (about 0.31% per week average, computed)
items.note: Sponsor topline as reported; not an approved drug

items.label: When loss is fastest
items.value: Faster in the first 6 months, then slows; plateau around 52 to 72 weeks; onset expected by 4 weeks
items.note: Sources do not give a per-week rate for the early months

items.label: Rapid loss and bone
items.value: Substantial (14%) and rapid (over 3 to 4 months) weight loss is associated with significant bone loss
items.note: Advisory statement; slower, moderate loss may better preserve bone

items.label: Lean mass share of weight lost
items.value: About 35 to 38% (semaglutide, STEP 1) and about 25% (tirzepatide, SURMOUNT-1); calorie restriction alone about 20 to 25%
items.note: Lean mass is not all muscle; functional impact unknown

items.label: Label response check (Saxenda only)
items.value: Stop if less than 5% of starting weight lost after 12 weeks on 3.0 mg
items.note: A labelled stopping rule; other products' monographs have no weekly-rate rule

items.label: After stopping a GLP-1 drug
items.value: About 1 to 2% regained at 4 weeks; about one-half to two-thirds of the loss regained at 1 year
items.note: BC PAD summary

tables.title: Rick's planned tiers compared with the evidence (example: 150 kg person)
rows: Trial averages were about 0.2 to 0.3% per week, so most trial participants would be flagged 'slow' by this tier
Above the NIH guideline pace (up to about 0.9 kg) and at or above the NIH gallstone-risk pace (over about 1.4 kg)
More than twice the gallstone-risk pace
tables.note: kg values are computed (150 kg x %). The planned tiers look high: the 'target' is faster than guidelines and faster than average GLP-1 trial results.

tables.title: Evidence-based default tiers (proposal for the app; review with a clinician)
rows: under 0.2% per week averaged over 4 or more weeks, after dose escalation
GLP-1 trial averages about 0.2 to 0.3% per week; app should not suggest dose changes (labels leave this to the prescriber)
0.2% to 0.75% per week AND no more than about 0.9 kg per week
Trial averages; NIH 0.5 to 2 lb per week
over 0.75% per week OR over 0.9 kg per week
over 1.4 kg (3 lb) per week sustained for 2 or more weeks
NIH gallstone-risk pace; also show gallbladder and dehydration warning signs
tables.note: The rolling-average idea and the 0.2% / 0.75% cut points are design choices derived from the cited figures, not thresholds stated by any guideline. Confidence: low to moderate.

statements.text: No guideline found sets a weekly percent target for GLP-1 therapy; guidelines describe absolute kg or lb per week for lifestyle weight loss, and trials report total percent change over 1 to 2 years.
The advisory says dietary recommendations should be adjusted based on the rate of weight reduction.

topics.topic: Energy: calorie estimates and calorie floors
topics.summary: Mifflin-St Jeor with actual body weight is the most reliable common equation, including in obesity; supervised care is needed below 800 kcal.

items.label: Mifflin-St Jeor, men (resting energy)
items.value: 10 x weight (kg) + 6.25 x height (cm) - 5 x age (y) + 5
items.note: Derived from 498 adults including 234 with obesity

items.label: Mifflin-St Jeor, women (resting energy)
items.value: 10 x weight (kg) + 6.25 x height (cm) - 5 x age (y) - 161
items.note: Same study

items.label: Accuracy of Mifflin-St Jeor
items.value: Most reliable common equation; within 10% of measured in about 70% of people with obesity (using actual weight)
items.note: Individual errors still occur; measured RMR (indirect calorimetry) is more accurate

items.label: Which weight to use with BMI 30 or more
items.value: Actual body weight
items.note: Using adjusted weight with Harris-Benedict increased errors (74% outside 10%); Mifflin with actual weight performed best

items.label: Activity multipliers
items.value: Not part of Mifflin-St Jeor; Health Canada's energy equations use activity categories by PAL: inactive 1.00-1.53, low active 1.53-1.68, active 1.68-1.85, very active 1.85-2.50
items.note: The common 1.2 to 1.9 multipliers were not found in the sources checked; Health Canada's EER equations are the sourced alternative

items.label: Health Canada on energy adequacy
items.value: Relative body weight (loss, stable, gain) is the preferred indicator of energy adequacy
items.note: EER equations are estimates; no separate adult equations for obesity

items.label: Typical calorie prescriptions for weight loss
items.value: 1,200 to 1,500 kcal/day for women; 1,500 to 1,800 kcal/day for men; or a 500 to 750 kcal/day deficit
items.note: 2013 AHA/ACC/TOS guideline; levels usually adjusted for body weight

items.label: Micronutrient risk at low intake
items.value: Higher risk of micronutrient inadequacy below 1,200 kcal/day (women) and 1,800 kcal/day (men)
items.note: Joint advisory statement

items.label: Very-low-calorie diets
items.value: Under 800 kcal/day only with trained practitioners and medical monitoring
items.note: AHA/ACC/TOS 2013; NICE: low-energy (800-1,200) and very-low-energy (<800) diets only in specialist services, nutritionally complete, no more than 12 weeks

items.label: Calorie reduction on GLP-1s
items.value: Observed intake reductions of 16% to 39% vs placebo
items.note: Joint advisory

topics.topic: Protein during weight loss and GLP-1 therapy
topics.summary: RDA 0.8 g/kg; 1.2 to 1.6 g/kg proposed during active loss; with obesity, an absolute 80 to 120 g/day avoids overestimating from body weight.

items.label: Health Canada RDA
items.value: 0.80 g/kg/day (reference 56 g/day men, 46 g/day women)
items.note: Set for weight-stable healthy adults

items.label: Proposed during active weight reduction
items.value: 1.2 to 1.6 g/kg/day
items.note: 'Have also been proposed'; not a formal recommendation; body-weight basis unclear

items.label: More accurate basis if body composition known
items.value: 1.5 g per kg of fat-free (lean) mass per day
items.note: Requires a body-composition measurement

items.label: Absolute target option
items.value: 80 to 120 g/day (16% to 24% of energy on a 2,000 kcal diet)
items.note: Advisory option that avoids overestimating from actual weight

items.label: Which body weight to use (BMI 30 or more)
items.value: Unclear; actual weight can significantly overestimate needs
items.note: Advisory caution; consider the absolute 80-120 g/day option

items.label: Lower limit
items.value: Should not fall below 0.4 to 0.5 g/kg/day
items.note: Advisory

items.label: Upper caution
items.value: Avoid prolonged intake at or above 2 g/kg/day
items.note: Advisory

items.label: Exercise to preserve muscle
items.value: Strength training at least 3 times weekly plus at least 150 minutes of moderate aerobic exercise weekly
items.note: Resistance training is linked to the least lean-mass loss (BC PAD)

statements.text: Obesity Canada (2025) recommends adequate nutritional and protein intake and regular physical activity to preserve muscle (as summarized by BC PAD).

topics.topic: Fluids, fibre and common GI problems on GLP-1 therapy
topics.summary: Dehydration from GI side effects is a labelled warning; meal size and fat strategies come from the 2025 advisory.

items.label: Total water (Health Canada AI)
items.value: 3.7 L/day men; 2.7 L/day women
items.note: Total water includes drinking water, beverages and water in food

items.label: Dehydration warning (Wegovy monograph)
items.value: Drink plenty of fluids to prevent dehydration when GI side effects occur
items.population: People on Wegovy (similar warnings in other GLP-1 monographs, see R1)
items.note: Dehydration can worsen kidney function

items.label: Meal pattern for nausea
items.value: Small breakfast, then additional small meals every 3 to 4 hours while drinking adequate fluids; vomiting is more likely with large meals
items.note: Advisory

items.label: Fat and fibre early on
items.value: Avoid fatty or high-fibre foods during the first few days of treatment; avoid large or high-fat meals for diarrhea
items.note: Advisory

items.label: Constipation
items.value: Advisory suggests daily magnesium supplementation titrated to keep bowel movements regular
items.note: Health Canada's UL for supplemental magnesium is 350 mg/day; discuss with a pharmacist

items.label: Alcohol
items.value: Should be minimized
items.note: Advisory

items.label: Dose escalation and GI effects
items.value: Escalation can be slowed or paused; severe or prolonged symptoms or abdominal pain should be investigated
items.note: BC PAD; trials let participants stay at a dose up to 8 weeks (advisory)

items.label: Malnutrition signs to watch
items.value: Weakness, faintness, fatigue, dry skin, irritability, trouble concentrating
items.note: BC PAD counselling points

topics.topic: Warning signs to contact a healthcare provider
topics.summary: Symptom wording from the Wegovy monograph's patient section and Canadian sources.

items.label: Gallstones
items.value: Sudden pain in the upper stomach or back, often on the right, with nausea, vomiting, indigestion or cramping
items.note: Listed as a serious side effect

items.label: Pancreatitis
items.value: Severe, ongoing pain in the stomach area
items.note: Listed as a serious side effect; professional monographs add pain that may spread to the back (see R1)

items.label: Severe low blood sugar
items.value: Confusion, fits, or passing out
items.population: People with type 2 diabetes, especially on insulin or a sulfonylurea

items.label: Acute kidney injury / dehydration
items.value: Swelling in legs, ankles or feet; tiredness; confusion; shortness of breath; not enough urine
items.population: People with vomiting, diarrhea or low fluid intake
items.note: Drink plenty of fluids to prevent dehydration

items.label: Severe allergic reaction
items.value: Breathing problems; swelling of face, lips, tongue or throat with trouble swallowing; fast heartbeat

items.label: Vision changes
items.value: Blurred or changing vision, vision loss, impaired colour vision; sudden vision loss (NAION, very rare)
items.population: People on GLP-1 drugs (retinopathy risk in type 2 diabetes)

items.label: Appendicitis (uncommon)
items.value: Sudden pain in the lower right abdomen, chills, fever, nausea or vomiting

items.label: Before surgery or sedation
items.value: Tell the healthcare professional you take a GLP-1 drug (risk of food or liquid entering the lungs)
items.population: Anyone having anesthesia or deep sedation
items.note: Health Canada 2026 safety review

items.label: Possible malnutrition
items.value: Weakness, faintness, fatigue, dry skin, irritability, trouble concentrating
items.population: People eating very little on GLP-1 drugs
items.note: BC PAD counselling

statements.text: The monograph's patient table marks which symptoms mean 'talk to your healthcare professional' and which mean 'stop taking and get immediate medical help'; the fetched text did not preserve those columns, so the app should show the product's own table wording.
